review:
Super Markup Man is one of those unusual indie projects that immediately stands out because of how strange its core idea sounds on paper. A platformer designed to teach HTML and CSS could have easily ended up feeling like a glorified classroom exercise, yet the game manages to avoid that trap through clever design and a surprisingly engaging gameplay loop. Instead of presenting coding concepts through dry tutorials or walls of text, the experience turns web development mechanics into interactive puzzles and environmental challenges. The result is a game that feels educational without constantly reminding the player that they are learning something practical along the way.

The game revolves around the use of HTML tags and CSS concepts as actual gameplay mechanics. Players move through stages while carrying and positioning markup elements that directly alter the environment. Rather than typing code manually, the game visualizes web design principles in ways that are easy to understand. Tags become tools that open paths, solve environmental puzzles, and manipulate stage layouts. This approach works remarkably well because it introduces coding concepts through experimentation instead of memorization. Players gradually begin understanding how various elements function together simply by interacting with the world around them.

One of the strongest aspects of Super Markup Man is the way it structures progression. Early levels are simple enough for newcomers to understand basic mechanics, but the complexity steadily increases as new systems are introduced. HTML-focused stages emphasize structure and organization, while CSS-oriented sections place more attention on visual manipulation, layout adjustments, and styling concepts. The game carefully balances challenge and accessibility, making sure that players are constantly learning without becoming overwhelmed. Even players with absolutely no prior knowledge of coding can follow the progression comfortably because the mechanics are introduced naturally through gameplay situations.

The puzzle design is more creative than many would expect from an educational title. Later stages become increasingly elaborate and require players to think logically about how different elements interact. Certain levels focus on timing and movement while others encourage experimentation and observation. Some puzzles initially seem confusing, but the eventual solution often creates a satisfying sense of understanding that mirrors solving an actual programming problem. That feeling of discovery is where the game becomes genuinely rewarding. It does not simply tell players how coding works; it encourages them to understand systems through problem solving.

Visually, the game embraces a bright and playful art direction that suits its educational tone perfectly. The colorful environments and clean interface make everything readable and approachable, which is especially important in a puzzle game built around learning mechanics. The character designs and animations are simple but charming enough to keep the presentation lively throughout the experience. While the graphics are not technically impressive compared to larger productions, they serve the gameplay effectively and maintain a welcoming atmosphere that fits the overall concept.

Another feature that deserves praise is the real-time page rendering system. As players complete puzzles and manipulate elements, they can see web pages visually forming through their actions. This immediate feedback creates a strong connection between gameplay and the coding concepts being taught. Abstract ideas suddenly become tangible because players can directly observe how modifications affect the outcome. It is an extremely smart educational design choice that reinforces learning without interrupting the pace of the game.

The inclusion of Bug Mode adds another layer of personality and creativity. Random bugs appear within levels, requiring players to locate and eliminate them before progressing. This mechanic acts as a playful representation of debugging in real programming, teaching players that errors and troubleshooting are natural parts of the development process. Instead of turning debugging into something frustrating, the game frames it as an entertaining challenge. It subtly introduces players to the mindset required in programming while maintaining the game’s lighthearted tone.

Free Play Mode also helps the game stand out from other educational titles. Players are given opportunities to experiment with creating their own layouts and exporting content as real HTML files. This transforms the experience from a simple puzzle-platformer into something closer to a genuine learning tool. Curious players can begin applying concepts outside the game itself, which speaks volumes about how effectively the mechanics teach foundational ideas. It is rare for an educational game to inspire actual interest in its subject matter, but Super Markup Man genuinely succeeds in making web design feel approachable and fun.

The cooperative functionality is another welcome addition, especially for parents, teachers, or friends who want to solve puzzles together. Cooperative play encourages communication and experimentation, which naturally strengthens the educational aspect of the game. While the multiplayer implementation is relatively straightforward, it adds extra replay value and makes the learning process feel more social and collaborative.

Of course, the game is not without flaws. Some later puzzles lean heavily into trial-and-error problem solving, which may occasionally frustrate players who are unfamiliar with logical coding structures. The platforming mechanics themselves are functional but not particularly deep, meaning players looking for highly refined movement systems may find the gameplay somewhat basic. Certain mechanics can also feel repetitive during longer sessions because the educational focus naturally limits how far the game can expand its ideas. However, these issues rarely overshadow the creativity and charm that define the overall experience.

What ultimately makes Super Markup Man memorable is how committed it is to combining entertainment and education in a meaningful way. The game never talks down to players, nor does it overwhelm them with unnecessary complexity. Instead, it introduces practical concepts through engaging gameplay and thoughtful puzzle design. It understands that curiosity and experimentation are the most effective teaching tools, and it builds its entire structure around that philosophy.

For players interested in coding, puzzle-platformers, or simply unique indie concepts, Super Markup Man offers something genuinely refreshing. It may not have the production values of major platforming titles, but its originality and educational creativity allow it to stand apart from countless generic indie releases. Few games manage to teach practical skills while remaining consistently entertaining, and that alone makes this project worthy of recognition.

Super Markup Man, herhangi bir kodlama becerisi gerektirmeden HTML ve CSS öğreten bir 2D bulmaca platform oyunudur. Roppy Chop Studios tarafından geliştirilen ve yayınlanan oyun 16 Ağustos 2016 tarihinde piyasaya sürülmüştür.

Oyun, oyuncuya A, IMG, STRONG ve EM gibi temel HTML etiketlerinin yanı sıra CSS modunda daha gelişmiş biçimlendirme ve stilleri aşamalı olarak tanıtan 100 seviye / alıştırma sunar. Oyunun mekaniği, bu etiketleri ekranın etrafında taşımak ve web sitenizin gerçek zamanlı olarak işlenmesini izlemek etrafında dönüyor. Oyuncu her seviyeyi geçmek için web sitesini önizleme ile eşleştirmelidir.

Ana oyun moduna ek olarak, oyun ayrıca oyuncuların seviyeleri gerçek HTML dosyalarına aktarabilecekleri bir Serbest Oyun modu sunar. Bu mod, oyuncuların öğrendikleri kodu denemelerine ve becerilerini daha da geliştirmelerine olanak tanır.

Oyunun ilginç bir özelliği, karmaşıklık katmanı ekleyen ve oyuncunun kodları hakkında eleştirel düşünmesini gerektiren isteğe bağlı "hata" ayarıdır. Ayrıca, Super Markup Man Free Play ve CSS modlarında yerel kooperatifi destekliyor, ancak ikinci oyuncunun bir gamepad (tercihen bir Xbox gamepad) kullanması gerekiyor.

Super Markup Man, Steam'deki 93 incelemenin tamamı çok olumlu olmak üzere son derece olumlu eleştiriler aldı. Oyun, web geliştirmeyi öğretmeye yönelik yenilikçi yaklaşımı ve ilgi çekici oynanışı nedeniyle övgüyle karşılandı. Bazı oyuncular oyunun zorluğunun zaman zaman zorlayıcı olabildiğini belirttiler, ancak bu, oyuncuları yaratıcı düşünmeye ve problem çözmeye teşvik ettiği için olumlu bir yön olarak görülüyor.

Genel olarak Super Markup Man, HTML ve CSS'yi eğlenceli ve ilgi çekici bir şekilde öğrenmek isteyen herkes için mükemmel bir oyundur. Oyunun mekanikleri sezgiseldir ve seviyeler aşamalı olarak birbiri üzerine inşa edilerek oyuncuların kendi hızlarında öğrenmelerini kolaylaştırır. İsteğe bağlı "bug" ayarı ve yerel kooperatif modu da oyuna derinlik katıyor ve oyuncuları oynamaya ve öğrenmeye devam etmeye teşvik ediyor.

I bought the game solely for the achievements as I already know HTML and CSS fairly well.

[h1]As an achievement hunting game[/h1]
It's quite simple. First you have to solve 50 levels with only HTML. After that, you have to solve another 50 levels with both HTML and CSS. After that you have to, i.a., play the free mode for 30 minutes, download a file that has a bug in it, solve levels in different ways and play the game in co-op (which can be done alone, I used a xbox controller. I didn't check if the other keys on your keyboard can be used).

[h1]As a game[/h1]
It's kind of ehhhh. Gameplay is tedious because you have to run around picking up tags to move them. Simple drag and drop mechanics would be a lot more fun. That, I believe, would also make it possible / easier to create more complex levels as you have more space to work with. I, however, did find some of the levels (lvl 40+) fun to solve, so it kind of works as a puzzle game although, like said, click and drag mechanics would make it less tedious. I also had fun trying to speedrun the game.

[h1]As a game that's supposed to teach HTML and CSS[/h1]
It's also kind of ehhhh. Sure, it shows you that you have to close tags in the correct order, but as long as that condition is met, the tags can be anywhere. It also doesn't explain what the tags do unless you open the help panel. You also don't see what you're supposed to do unless you press CTRL, and if you do that, you can't see your own progress.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

[*]For achievement hunting? Sure, although it might take some time if you are not familiar with HTML and CSS.
[*]As a game? Meh, there's lot of better ones.
[*]As a learning method/app/game: Meh, just google for some tutorials.

Как вы все знаете, HTML используется как язык описания любых веб-страниц, хоть бы и той, на которой вы читаете этот обзор.
В то время как управлять человечком просто забавно и несложно, основное время и силы уходят на решение текущего паззла. Все они состоят в том, что необходимо выстроить все HTML теги так, чтобы результат, на лету отображаемый в специальном поле, соответствовал тому, что задан уровнем. Тут всё достаточно легко -- специальных знаний заранее не требуется, по первым уровням можно догадаться логически, как выстраиваются те или иные элементы, дальше будет постепенное усложнение. Некоторые теги, особенно, вложенные, могут вызвать вопросы у новичков, тогда придётся обращаться за помощью в поисковик. 50 имеющихся уровней проходятся довольно быстро, после этого открывается раздел с CSS.

CSS - язык описания стилей. Опять же, текущая страница вся использует CSS, он отвечает за внешний вид HTML тегов, и именно он делает все сайты, использующие одни и те же теги, "разными", на вкус и цвет.
По игре, CSS уже несколько усложняет работу -- помимо тех же тегов, с которыми вы работали ранее, появится доп. башня с полицейским, который будет переставлять блоки со стилями, поэтому работы прибавится в два раза. Он не имеет ничего общего с HTML, и будет несколько сложно сразу понять, как именно с ним надо работать, если вы ранее таким не занимались. Но, к чести разработчика, сильного усложнения он не допускал, так что теоретически можно пройти эти 50 уровней не имея специальных знаний.

As someone who is already very familiar with both HTML and CSS, I bought and played this game purely so I could review it, and possibly recommend it to friends who wanted to learn. I will not be doing the latter. This game is honestly a really bad way to teach anyone HTML or CSS, due to both the way it tries to teach and the way it plays as a game. The game doesn't attempt to explain anything regarding what tags do, and how they should be used. It simply tosses them on the screen and expects the player to arrange them properly. In a way this is fine if the player is someone who learns better by trying to figure things out for themselves, but further issues ruin that potential. The player is never expected to type anything, instead all that they do is move blocks with words and tags around. This too would be fine, if it weren't for the fact that you can place blocks on top of each other in odd fashions that muddies the flow of the HTML so its difficult to understand what should be displayed. Furthermore, you can place the tags anywhere instead of the game encouraging any kind of neat arrangement. [code] text [/code] This would result in a success even though all the tags are scattered about. This kind of arrangement is not a good thing to teach. To make it worse the game makes a point of saying it's trying to teach the proper way of doing things. Now as to why it's a bad GAME aside from being an educational tool. The UI and visuals are absolutely rubbish. The game should be displaying both the page preview and the goal at the same time, rather than the player needing to switch between the two. Additionally, the 'hints' should just be displayed all the time, as they're often information the player should know regardless of trying to work out the puzzle. The gameplay is also tedious and irritating. You have to jump around the screen picking up and dropping the blocks, when simply dropping and dragging with a mouse would have been much more sensible and less pointlessly time consuming. Even worse, if you drop a block on top of another, it can become difficult to pick up unless you position the character correctly. Overall, don't buy this. There are better ways to learn and teach HTML/CSS.
